title: AMAT 计算器：多级嵌套与命中率敏感性
expected_output:
=== AMAT of a 3-level cache hierarchy ===
  main memory access time = 200 cycles

  lvl    hit time     hit rate         AMAT
  L1            1          95%         2.10
  L2           10          80%        22.00
  L3           40          90%        60.00

  so a load costs 2.10 cycles on average
  (the L1 'miss penalty' is really the L2 AMAT: 22.0 cycles)

=== sensitivity: how much does a small hit-rate drop cost? ===
  assume L1 hit time 1 cycle, flat miss penalty 100 cycles

   L1 hit rate         AMAT
         99.9%         1.10
         99.0%         2.00
         98.0%         3.00
         95.0%         6.00
         90.0%        11.00
         80.0%        21.00

reading the table:
  99%% -> 2 cycles, 95%% -> 6 cycles.  4 percentage points = 3x slowdown.
  this is why cache optimisations are worth real engineering effort,
  and why the multiplier (miss rate) matters more than the addend (hit time).

=== what if the miss penalty is halved instead? ===
      hit rate  penalty 100   penalty 50
         99.0%         2.00         1.50
         95.0%         6.00         3.50
  halving the miss penalty helps, but raising the hit rate is usually cheaper
  (better data layout costs no new hardware)
code:
def amat(levels, mem_time):
    """levels = [(hit_time, local_hit_rate), ...] 由外到内；返回各级 AMAT
       采用口径：缺失代价 = 下一级的 AMAT（命中时间已包含在下一级里）"""
    # 从最内层往外递推
    t = mem_time
    out = []
    for hit, h in reversed(levels):
        t = hit + (1 - h) * t
        out.append((hit, h, t))
    return list(reversed(out))          # 还原成 由外到内

print("=== AMAT of a 3-level cache hierarchy ===")
LEV = [(1, 0.95), (10, 0.80), (40, 0.90)]     # L1, L2, L3
MEM = 200
res = amat(LEV, MEM)
print("  main memory access time = %d cycles" % MEM)
print()
print("  %-4s %10s %12s %12s" % ("lvl", "hit time", "hit rate", "AMAT"))
names = ["L1", "L2", "L3"]
for nm, (hit, h, t) in zip(names, res):
    print("  %-4s %10d %11.0f%% %12.2f" % (nm, hit, 100 * h, t))
print()
print("  so a load costs %.2f cycles on average" % res[0][2])
print("  (the L1 'miss penalty' is really the L2 AMAT: %.1f cycles)" % (res[1][2] - res[1][0] + res[1][0]))
print()

print("=== sensitivity: how much does a small hit-rate drop cost? ===")
print("  assume L1 hit time 1 cycle, flat miss penalty 100 cycles")
print()
print("  %12s %12s" % ("L1 hit rate", "AMAT"))
for h in (0.999, 0.99, 0.98, 0.95, 0.90, 0.80):
    print("  %11.1f%% %12.2f" % (100 * h, 1 + (1 - h) * 100))
print()
print("reading the table:")
print("  99%% -> 2 cycles, 95%% -> 6 cycles.  4 percentage points = 3x slowdown.")
print("  this is why cache optimisations are worth real engineering effort,")
print("  and why the multiplier (miss rate) matters more than the addend (hit time).")

print()
print("=== what if the miss penalty is halved instead? ===")
print("  %12s %12s %12s" % ("hit rate", "penalty 100", "penalty 50"))
for h in (0.99, 0.95):
    a = 1 + (1 - h) * 100
    b = 1 + (1 - h) * 50
    print("  %11.1f%% %12.2f %12.2f" % (100 * h, a, b))
print("  halving the miss penalty helps, but raising the hit rate is usually cheaper")
print("  (better data layout costs no new hardware)")
